title: All gluing coefficients occur at the selected stage
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with its selected finite affine gluing presentation $\mathsf G_S$ [def-nagata-finite-affine-gluing-presentation], and use the marked record, compatible coefficient index set $I(\mathsf G_S)$, finite seed $(E_P)_P$, selected indices $i_a$, and stage $\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}$ of [def-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficient-stage]. Write $A_P=\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_S)$ for each marked affine ring and $B_P=B_{P,\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}}\subseteq A_P$. These are the finite affine subring models of [def-nagata-finite-affine-subring-model]. Each selected coefficient subalgebra $B_{P,i_a}$ is contained in $B_P$ via the specified transition inclusion. All selected seed coefficients and basic-open elements belong to their respective $B_P$, and every recorded restricted overlap map and proposed reverse map is defined on the indicated small rings and their localizations at this stage. Each such map is the restriction of the corresponding original map. Explicitly, for a principal-open piece $p:a\to b$ with original ring map $\rho_p:A_b\to(A_a)_{f_p}$, its small map $\rho_{p,0}:B_b\to(B_a)_{f_p}$ obeys
$$j_{a,f_p}\rho_{p,0}=\rho_pj_b,$$
where $j_a:B_a\to A_a$ and $j_b:B_b\to A_b$ are the chart-ring inclusions and $j_{a,f_p}$ is the induced inclusion into the original localization [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The original marked opens are recovered by chartwise base change; for a principal-open piece the canonical isomorphism is $(B_a)_{f_p}\otimes_{B_a}A_a\simeq(A_a)_{f_p}$, sending $(b/f_p^m)\otimes x$ to $j_a(b)x/f_p^m$. Together with this recovery, these comparison equations identify all the selected raw data with the corresponding restrictions of $\mathsf G_S$.

proof.text: Use the finite marked record and compatible coefficient index set of [def-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficient-stage], with models as in [def-nagata-finite-affine-subring-model]. Its order is componentwise subring inclusion; each index is an actual tuple of finitely generated integer subrings with the prescribed original restrictions. The finite affine presentation [def-nagata-finite-affine-gluing-presentation] gives finitely many main charts. The stage construction assigns each marked affine $P$ to one main chart $a$, partitions the seed into families $E^{(a)}$, chooses $i_a$ containing that family, and sets $F=\{i_\varnothing\}\cup\{i_a:1\leq a\leq n\}$ and $\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}=u(F)$. Thus $F$ is a finite subset of the same constructed directed set.

source.place: ## Proof: common coefficient bound and recovery, interpreted with the reviewed compatible coefficient-system definition (order 334)

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound] to $F$: every $i_a\leq\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}$. If $e\in E_P$, let $a$ be the chart to which $P$ was assigned. The selection in [def-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficient-stage] gives $e\in B_{P,i_a}$. Componentwise inclusion along $i_a\leq\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}$ gives $e\in B_{P,\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}}=B_P$. Every marked basic-open element is included in the initial seed by that definition, so these elements are also defined at the same stage. The same componentwise inclusion sends the entire selected subalgebra $B_{P,i_a}$ into $B_P$, so the selected coefficient subalgebras, and not just their seed elements, are simultaneously represented there. For $n=0$ the marked record is empty and $F=\{i_\varnothing\}$; the element and map assertions are vacuous.

source.place: ## Proof: common coefficient bound and recovery, interpreted with the reviewed compatible coefficient-system definition (order 334)

proof.text: For any actual subring $B\subseteq A$ and $f\in B$, define the fraction map $j_f:B_f\to A_f$ by $b/f^n\mapsto b/f^n$. It is well defined: a witness $f^k(bf^m-cf^n)=0$ in $B$ is also a witness in $A$. Conversely, equality of the image fractions supplies such a witness in $A$ by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. All elements in that equality belong to the actual subring $B$, so the equality holds in $B$, proving injectivity. The fraction addition and multiplication formulas show that $j_f$ preserves sums, products and $1$. This justifies identifying localized model subrings with their images, even when $f$ is a zero divisor or nilpotent.

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization), preceding fraction-equivalence construction and fraction operations

proof.text: Evaluate the tuple at $\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}$. Clauses 1 and 2 of [def-nagata-finite-affine-subring-model] say that every original restriction and recorded localized comparison, including its reverse, preserves the indicated small rings; its small map is this restriction. For a recorded basic open $P=D_{U_a}(f_p)$, its recorded list is the singleton $\{f_p\}$. The unit-ideal certificate gives $c\rho(f_p)=1$ in $B_P$, so localization at $\rho(f_p)$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $z/\rho(f_p)^m\mapsto zc^m$. Composing its inverse with the model localization isomorphism identifies $(B_a)_{f_p}$ with $B_P$. Thus the piece map into chart $b$ has type $\rho_{p,0}:B_b\to(B_a)_{f_p}$. For every $x\in B_b$, its value is the original $\rho_p(j_b(x))$ viewed in the localized small subring; applying $j_{a,f_p}$ proves the stated comparison equation. More generally, let $\psi:C\to D$ be any recorded localized comparison or its reverse, with small restriction $\psi_0:C_0\to D_0$ and inclusions $j_C,j_D$. On $y=x/d^m\in C_0$, one has $j_D(\psi_0(y))=\psi(j_C(y))=\psi(x)/\psi(d)^m$, so $j_D\psi_0=\psi j_C$. For several denominators use their product; for an unlocalized source take $m=0$. Finally for $i\leq j$, the two transition composites for such a comparison both send $x/d^m$ to $\psi(x)/\psi(d)^m$ in the original target localization. Injectivity from step 3 makes them equal in the small target. These are precisely the fraction transition maps specified in [def-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficient-stage].

source.place: ## Proof: common coefficient bound and recovery, interpreted with the reviewed compatible coefficient-system definition (order 334)

proof.text: For a principal-open piece apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-localization-away-base-change] with $R=A=B_a$, the other algebra $B=A_a$, and $g=f_p$. Its canonical isomorphism, after the elementary identification $B_a\otimes_{B_a}A_a\simeq A_a$ given by $b\otimes x\mapsto j_a(b)x$, with inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ (the tensor balancing relation verifies both composites), gives $(B_a)_{f_p}\otimes_{B_a}A_a\simeq(A_a)_{f_p}$, with $(b/f_p^n)\otimes a\mapsto ba/f_p^n$. Thus original principal-open pieces are recovered by chartwise base change. For a general marked inclusion $P\subseteq Q$, the coefficient-stage statement [def-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficient-stage] specifies its image as the prescribed finite union of these basic opens, with the same fraction identifications on intersections, and explicitly supplies its inverse-image/pullback comparison with the original marked open. Apply this to every marked inclusion. Together with the elementwise comparison equations in step 4, it identifies the original restricted overlap maps and proposed reverse maps with the selected raw data at the coefficient stage.

blueprint_update.statement:
Every selected finite coefficient subalgebra, basic-open element, restricted
overlap map, and proposed inverse is defined at
$\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}$. Under base change to the original chart rings,
these objects are the corresponding restrictions of the data in
$\mathsf G_S$.

proof.text:
Each finite coefficient list lies in one finitely generated
$\mathbf Z$-subalgebra by
[lemma-nagata-ring-finite-type-subalgebras]. The selected upper bound
dominates every such stage by
[lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound]. Hence all selected
coefficients and restricted maps are simultaneously defined at the named
common stage, and base change returns the original finite lists. The full
chart rings are recovered only after taking the filtered colimit over all
finite refinements; no single stage is asserted to contain every coefficient
of an arbitrary chart ring.
